security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline formatting, Chinese text, and legitimate diagnostic terminology. However, the skill directs the agent to execute infrastructure commands without explicit approval boundaries for privileged or state-changing work. Add scope validation, approval, secret-handling, and rollback requirements before publication.

remediation.issue: State-changing and privileged operations lack an explicit approval gate.
remediation.suggestion: Require user approval after presenting each command, target, impact, rollback plan, and verification method.

remediation.issue: The workflow does not require read-only diagnostics or target validation before execution.
remediation.suggestion: Default to read-only checks, verify the environment and resource scope, then use least-privilege credentials.

remediation.issue: Secret and key management capabilities have no handling safeguards.
remediation.suggestion: Prohibit printing secrets, use approved secret stores, redact outputs, and confirm rotation or revocation steps.

content.user_title: Operate Infrastructure with an Ops Engineer
content.value_statement: Infrastructure operations can be risky, fragmented, and difficult to troubleshoot. This skill structures deployment, diagnostics, automation, monitoring, and recovery into an executable workflow.
actual_capabilities: Creates plans for Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, Ansible, Nginx, and CI/CD configurations.
Guides system, container, network, and application troubleshooting with standard diagnostic tools.
Designs Prometheus collection, alert rules, Grafana dashboards, and log pipelines.
Prepares Shell or Python automation scripts, scheduled jobs, and infrastructure configuration.
Supports security maintenance, certificate management, key rotation, and baseline checks.
Structures backup scripts, filesystem snapshots, disaster recovery plans, and operational records.
limitations: The package contains guidance only and provides no tested scripts, templates, or provider integrations.
Execution requires user-provided tools, credentials, connectivity, permissions, and environment context.
Privileged or state-changing commands can disrupt live systems without explicit review and approval.
Recommendations remain generic until the user supplies platform, topology, policy, and recovery requirements.

use_cases.title: Deploy a Containerized Service
use_cases.description: Prepare deployment files, health checks, validation steps, and rollback guidance for a new service.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a Production Incident
use_cases.description: Collect read-only evidence, identify likely causes, propose controlled fixes, and document verification results.

use_cases.title: Build a Delivery Pipeline
use_cases.description: Define build, test, image, and deployment stages for GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, or Jenkins.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Server Symptom
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this server issue: [symptoms]. Ask for missing context, propose read-only checks first, explain expected results, and stop before making changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner diagnosis of CPU, memory, disk, or network problems.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Container Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a [Docker Compose or Kubernetes] deployment for [service]. Include dependencies, health checks, secrets, observability, validation, rollback, and approval points.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate deployment planning for a containerized application.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a Kubernetes Outage
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose [cluster symptom] in [environment]. Order read-only evidence collection, rank hypotheses, propose minimal fixes, and define rollback and success criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced incident response for Kubernetes workloads.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Controlled Platform Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a migration from [current platform] to [target platform]. Include dependencies, staged execution, security controls, observability, failure gates, rollback, and recovery testing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert planning for a high-impact infrastructure change.

output_examples.input: A production server has sustained high load and slow responses.
output: Assessment: Separate CPU saturation, memory pressure, storage latency, and connection growth before selecting a fix.
Checks: Review load, process usage, memory, disk capacity, I/O latency, connections, and recent kernel or application errors.
Change gate: Present the likely cause, proposed command, impact, and rollback before changing the server.
Verification: Compare response time, resource use, errors, and service health after the approved change.

output_examples.input: A Kubernetes pod repeatedly enters CrashLoopBackOff.
output: Assessment: Common causes include configuration errors, startup failures, failed probes, missing dependencies, or resource limits.
Checks: Review pod details, previous container logs, recent events, exit codes, probes, and resource limits.
Change gate: Recommend the smallest fix and explain deployment impact and rollback before applying it.
Verification: Confirm stable running status, healthy probes, expected traffic, and clean logs.

output_examples.input: A team needs a GitLab CI pipeline that deploys to Kubernetes.
output: Pipeline plan: Separate build, test, image publication, deployment, and verification stages.
Security plan: Use protected credentials, restricted runners, image scanning, and environment approvals.
Release plan: Use staged deployment, health checks, observable success criteria, and a documented rollback path.

best_practices: Begin with read-only discovery and verify the target environment before any change.
Present commands, expected impact, approval points, rollback steps, and validation criteria.
Use least privilege, redact sensitive output, and store credentials in approved secret systems.
anti_patterns: Do not run privileged, destructive, or production commands without explicit user approval.
Do not guess resource names, clusters, accounts, regions, credentials, or recovery requirements.
Do not expose secrets in prompts, generated files, command histories, logs, or reports.

faq.question: Which operations domains does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers infrastructure, containers, Kubernetes, CI/CD, monitoring, troubleshooting, automation, security maintenance, backups, and disaster recovery.

faq.question: Does the skill include ready-to-run scripts?
faq.answer: No. The package contains operational guidance and examples, but it includes no tested scripts or configuration templates.

faq.question: Can it execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: Execution depends on the host agent, available tools, credentials, permissions, and user approval.

faq.question: Does it support Kubernetes troubleshooting?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes pod inspection, log and event analysis, resource checks, corrective changes, and verification.

faq.question: How should production changes be handled?
faq.answer: Use read-only checks first, verify scope, obtain approval, apply the smallest change, and keep a tested rollback path.

faq.question: Is secret management included?
faq.answer: The skill mentions secrets and key rotation. Users must provide secure storage, redaction, access controls, and rotation policies.
